practice1.prompt: Define an exception class InvalidAgeError built on Exception, then write validate_age(age) that raises it when the age is below 0 or above 150 and returns the age otherwise. Print validate_age(30)

cases.name: a valid age comes straight back

hiddenCases.name: an age at the edge is still valid
the error is a class of its own and is actually raised
hiddenCases.describe: class InvalidAgeError(Exception) and a raise that uses it

practice1.hint: Printing a complaint and carrying on leaves the caller holding the bad age and no way to know it. Raising hands the problem back to whoever asked, which is the only one who can decide what to do about it.

questions.prompt: Why raise an exception instead of printing a message and returning?
choices: The caller cannot tell a printed complaint from a good result, but it cannot ignore an exception
You cannot print inside a function
questions.explain: A message goes to a human. An exception goes to the code, which is what has to stop and do something differently.

questions.prompt: What must a custom exception class inherit from?
choices: Exception, or something that already inherits from it
questions.explain: raise only accepts exception types. A class that inherits from Exception is what makes it one.

questions.prompt: Why write InvalidAgeError instead of using ValueError?
choices: A caller can catch just this problem without catching every other bad value in the program
questions.explain: The type is the label. A name of its own is what lets one except clause mean this and not everything vaguely like it.
The base class is what makes it an exception, and raise is what actually stops the function and hands it to the caller.

questions.prompt: What does a bare `raise` inside an except block do?
choices: Re-raises the exception being handled, keeping its original traceback
questions.explain: It is how you log or clean up and still let the error carry on to whoever can actually deal with it.

reflection-exercise1.hint: Describe a moment where the function has been asked for something impossible, and say why returning any value at all would be a lie.

reflection-exercise2.hint: Think about the except clause someone else will write. What does your own class let them say that ValueError does not?
